strengths.explanation: In 2024, real GDP was 18 percent higher than in 2019, representing a compound annual growth rate of 3.4 percent.

strengths.item: Sound, well-capitalized, and liquid banking sector
strengths.explanation: Aggregate solvency and liquidity ratios stand at 15.0 and 54.7 percent at end-December 2024, respectively, which are almost double the regulatory requirements.

strengths.item: Resilient external position and current account surplus
strengths.explanation: The 2024 current account registered a surplus of 1.9 percent of GDP as a result of trade surpluses from the Colon Free Zone and export-processing zones.
Following 2023-24 restrictions, the Panama Canal returned to operating at full capacity in September 2024, handling an average of 36 ships per day.
Post-pandemic inflationary pressures have abated, with inflation turning negative to reach -0.7 percent year-on-year in May 2025.

strengths.item: Adequate bank asset quality and provisions
strengths.explanation: Non-performing loan ratios remain modest at 2.3 percent, and provisions amount to 102 percent of non-performing loans.

vulnerabilities.item: Deterioration in public finances and fiscal deficit
vulnerabilities.explanation: The 2024 non-financial public sector fiscal deficit reached 7.4 percent of GDP, up from a revised 3.9 percent of GDP in 2023.

vulnerabilities.item: Adverse economic impact of the mine closure
vulnerabilities.explanation: The closure of the Cobre Panamá copper mine contributed to GDP growth slowing from 7.3 percent in 2023 to 2.9 percent in 2024.
Debt of the non-financial public sector increased to 57.6 percent of GDP in 2024, up from 51.5 percent in 2023.
Following considerable fiscal deterioration in 2024 and rating downgrades, Panama faces significant downside risks regarding the loss of investment grade.
Arbitration proceedings over the Cobre Panamá closure could potentially result in large damages awards against the Panamanian State if negotiations are unsuccessful.
Significant disparities persist between urban areas like Panama City and Colón and rural areas and comarcas that depend on lower-productivity agriculture and subsistence farming.
